headline: High risk: shared filesystem and broad write/network privileges make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and shares state via a shared git repo; Open Interpreter can access the entire local filesystem and clipboard. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if one agent consumes the other's outputs as trusted text. No MCP/shared parser is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Aider reads files produced by Open Interpreter as instructions without sanitization
IF Open Interpreter copies Aider-generated text from clipboard into an execution prompt
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate repos/workspaces
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Require a human review step before either agent executes text from the other
Prefix inter-agent files with a strict data-only format
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and parser hardening

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history, while Open Interpreter can access the entire user filesystem and broad network egress. In default use, either agent can expose sensitive local files or repo contents through model-provider calls or outputs. The pair therefore creates a realistic exfiltration path with irreversible disclosure risk.
conditions: IF either agent is pointed at a directory containing secrets, credentials, or private documents
IF either agent sends file contents to its configured model provider
mitigations: Restrict both agents to a scrubbed workspace
Remove secrets from the shared filesystem before use
Disable network egress for one or both agents during sensitive tasks
Use separate OS users for the two agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory allowlists and secret scanning

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, write the filesystem, and modify git state. Aider shares state via a shared git repo, while Open Interpreter shares state via the filesystem. Concurrent edits to the same repo or files can overwrite each other or corrupt git history without locking, which is a direct write-conflict pathway.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or working tree
IF both agents write to the same files without external locking
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree
Serialize write access with a human coordinator
Pause one agent while the other commits
Use git worktrees for isolation
requires-engineering: add file-level locking and merge arbitration

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code edits and commits, and Open Interpreter can act on local files and execute shell commands. If Open Interpreter treats Aider's output as authoritative, an error can cascade from code suggestion to destructive local action or commit. The default action-taking authority makes this more than a simple review loop.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter executes commands or edits based on Aider output without verification
IF Aider-generated code is copied into Open Interpreter's execution context
mitigations: Require explicit verification before execution
Limit Open Interpreter to read-only review mode
Have Aider emit patch diffs only, not prose instructions
Review all commands in a human approval step
requires-engineering: add structured handoff schemas and validation

E_compliance.rationale: Aider is scoped to source code and git history, while Open Interpreter can touch anything reachable on the local machine. If regulated data lives on the same machine, Open Interpreter's broader access can violate residency or retention expectations relative to Aider's narrower repo scope. The other agent is cited because the mismatch is between their data scopes.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or secrets are stored on the local machine alongside the repo
IF retention or deletion rules differ between repo data and general filesystem data
mitigations: Keep regulated data off the shared machine
Use separate storage locations for repo and personal files
Document retention rules for each agent
Restrict Open Interpreter to a compliant directory
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls
